papers.title: Global Research Trends and Insights on AI Usage in Tuberculosis: Bibliometric Analysis.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health challenge despite prevention efforts. AI offers promising approaches to long-standing challenges in TB diagnosis, drug resistance detection, and case management; however, a systematic mapping of global research priorities and translational gaps in AI applications to TB is currently lacking.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis systematically maps global research trends and priorities in AI applications for tuberculosis, covering areas such as diagnosis, drug resistance detection, and case management. It identifies translational gaps between AI research output and clinical implementation in TB care. The study provides a landscape view of where AI research in TB is concentrated and where it is lacking.

papers.title: From QSAR to deep learning: an interpretable comprehensive pipeline with a read-across approach for mutagenicity prediction via the Enalos Cloud Platform.
papers.abstract: Assessing the mutagenicity of chemical compounds is essential for ensuring their safe handling and use, thereby minimizing potential health risks. New approach methodologies (NAMs), including computational approaches, provide non-animal alternatives for testing novel materials and chemicals. This study highlights the potential of in silico NAMs, which can contribute to the development of novel Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) chemicals and substances by identifying potentially hazardous ones at an early stage. Emphasis is given to the mutagenicity prediction based on data from the Ames (b
papers.summary: This paper presents an integrated computational pipeline combining QSAR modeling, deep learning, and read-across approaches to predict chemical mutagenicity, deployed via the Enalos Cloud Platform. The tool aims to support non-animal safety assessment of chemicals by identifying potentially hazardous compounds early in development, aligned with Safe and Sustainable by Design principles.

papers.title: Decision-grade evidence for AI-enabled small-molecule discovery.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence now guides choices across small-molecule discovery, yet benchmark gains rarely reveal whether a model changed the next compound, assay or project decision. This Perspective organizes public evidence around Design, Make, Test and Analyze (DMTA) handoffs. It distinguishes reproducible benchmark evidence (C1), use-relevant retrospective robustness (C2), executed Make or Test handoffs (C3), prospective workflow comparisons (C4-W) and traceable downstream trajectories (C4-D), with separate Evaluation, Deliverability and Governance profiles. Two authors independently screened
papers.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
papers.summary: This perspective argues that AI models in small-molecule discovery are usually judged by benchmark performance rather than whether they actually changed real project decisions. It proposes a tiered evidence framework (C1–C4) organized around Design-Make-Test-Analyze handoffs, distinguishing reproducible benchmarks from executed handoffs and prospective workflow comparisons, with separate profiles for evaluation, deliverability, and governance.

papers.title: Cross-docking and redocking reveal distinct determinants of success in physics-based and AI-driven binding pose prediction in protein-ligand complexes.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand pose prediction is central to structure-based drug discovery, yet the relative performance of physics-based and AI-driven methods under realistic cross-docking conditions remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we compare physics-based docking methods (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, and DOCK 6) with data-driven approaches, including the deep-learning model GNINA 1.3 and the diffusion-based frameworks AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, and DiffDock. Performance was evaluated using standardised redocking and cross-docking protocols across three Alzheimer's disease targets representing distinct
papers.summary: This study benchmarks physics-based docking tools (AutoDock4, Vina, DOCK 6) against AI-driven pose predictors (GNINA 1.3, AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, DiffDock) under both redocking and cross-docking conditions on three Alzheimer's disease targets. The authors find that the two method classes have distinct determinants of success, with performance diverging between the easier redocking scenario and the more realistic cross-docking setting. The work highlights that AI methods do not uniformly outperform physics-based docking and that benchmarking protocols strongly influence conclusions.

papers.title: Revisiting the LSER Approach in the Era of Machine Learning: Insights from IAM Chromatography.
papers.abstract: The present study demonstrates the integration of the linear solvation energy relationship (LSER) concept with machine learning (ML) methodologies to improve the predictive and interpretative capabilities of chromatographic retention modeling. Immobilized artificial membrane (IAM) chromatography was employed as a model biochromatographic system, and an in-house library of 993 structurally diverse compounds, with experimentally determined chromatographic hydrophobicity index of IAM (CHIIAM), was used to train LSER-ML models. LSER descriptors were calculated using Absolv and extended with ioniza
papers.summary: This study combines linear solvation energy relationship (LSER) descriptors with machine learning to predict chromatographic retention on immobilized artificial membrane (IAM) columns, using a library of 993 diverse compounds. The hybrid LSER-ML approach improves both predictive accuracy and interpretability compared to traditional LSER models. It demonstrates how classical physicochemical descriptors can be integrated with modern ML for biochromatographic modeling.

papers.title: A deep learning framework for oligopeptide candidate discovery across metabolism-related contexts.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods are increasingly critical in therapeutic peptide discovery but have been concentrated in certain applications, such as the development of antimicrobial peptides. Therapeutic peptide discovery in contexts such as metabolism, endocrinology, and tissue regeneration remains challenging due to a paucity of available indication-specific training data. Here, we propose a deep learning-based pipeline, Deepeptide, capable of identifying candidate oligopeptides for various metabolism-related contexts. Leveraging the intrinsic relationships between disease indic
papers.summary: The authors present Deepeptide, a deep learning pipeline that identifies candidate therapeutic oligopeptides for metabolism-related conditions such as metabolic disorders, endocrinology, and tissue regeneration, where training data are scarce. The framework leverages intrinsic relationships between disease indications to overcome the lack of indication-specific training data. This extends AI-driven peptide discovery beyond well-explored areas like antimicrobial peptides.

papers.title: From chemical space to synthetic reality: A framework for makeable-by-design generative AI in drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping molecular design, but many outputs are still judged by proxy metrics that do not establish whether proposed compounds can be synthesized, tested and advanced. This review reframes the field around 'synthetic reality': the extent to which AI-generated molecules survive route planning, precursor availability, experimental execution and medicinal chemistry decision-making. We examine the limits of heuristic synthesizability metrics, assess route-aware and execution-facing systems and propose maturity levels, reporting standards, actionability m
papers.summary: This review argues that generative AI in drug discovery should be evaluated not just by proxy metrics like synthesizability scores, but by whether proposed molecules can actually be synthesized, tested, and advanced in practice. It examines the limits of current heuristic metrics, reviews route-aware and execution-facing systems, and proposes maturity levels and reporting standards for 'makeable-by-design' generative AI.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and ultra-high performance computing methods and experiments for drug discovery: virtual screening, deep learning, molecular dynamics simulations, ADMET modelling, and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Recent years have witnessed considerable progress in computer-aided drug discovery, driven by the incorporation of computational technologies within both academic and pharmaceutical environments. This evolution is marked by a significant accumulation of data pertaining to detailed three-dimensional structural information, ligand properties, and their interactions with therapeutic targets. The augmentation of computational capabilities and the accessibility of extensive chemical libraries containing billions of drug-like small molecules have further facilitated this transition. To effectively u
papers.summary: This review surveys the integration of AI and ultra-high-performance computing across the drug discovery pipeline, covering virtual screening, deep learning, molecular dynamics simulations, and ADMET modeling, with experimental validation. It highlights how massive chemical libraries and detailed structural data are being leveraged computationally to accelerate hit identification and lead optimization. The paper serves as a broad overview of current computational strategies and their practical translation into experimental workflows.

papers.title: From diligence to verification: the emergence of the TechBio-Investor.
papers.abstract: Recent technical advances, including AI co-scientists and agentic systems, increasingly allow TechBios to undertake scientific verification at scale. In addition to facilitating internal discovery efforts, these capabilities can also be used for making external investment decisions. The emerging synergies between discovery and investment enable a new type of hybrid entity, the TechBio-Investor, which has the potential to reshape the economics and ethics of biotech investing. Scaled verification can help improve capital allocation, steering investment toward stronger science and, in a sector wh
papers.summary: This commentary argues that AI co-scientists and agentic systems now let TechBio companies perform scientific verification at scale, both for internal drug discovery and for evaluating external investments. This convergence creates a new hybrid entity, the 'TechBio-Investor,' which could reshape the economics and ethics of biotech investing by steering capital toward stronger science.

papers.title: Expanding Quantitative Medicines' Reach: Systems and Methods to Enhance R&D Productivity and Decision-Making in the Agentic-Era.
papers.abstract: Despite integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into drug discovery and an expanding global medicines pipeline, new drug approvals have declined, highlighting a paradox in biopharma: More drugs discovered, but less approvals, higher costs, and longer timelines. Reasons for the decreased research and development (R&D) efficiency are multifactorial, in part driven by the complexity of new modalities, difficult targets and indications, and persistence of cognitive biases in clinical decision-making. One proposed solution to address R&D productivity challenges includes the adoption of organiza
papers.summary: This perspective examines the paradox in biopharma where AI-driven drug discovery has expanded the pipeline yet new drug approvals have declined amid rising costs and longer timelines. The authors attribute this to multifactorial R&D inefficiency, including complex new modalities, difficult targets, and persistent cognitive biases in clinical decision-making. They propose adopting organizational systems and methods—framed around the emerging 'agentic era' of AI—to enhance R&D productivity and decision-making.

papers.title: Decoupling topological and molecular features for interpretable biomolecular interaction prediction.
papers.abstract: Predicting biomolecular interactions is fundamental to understanding cellular mechanisms and advancing drug discovery. However, biomolecular interactions exhibit immense diversity across multiple dimensions. Most existing computational methods are designed to handle one specific task or data modality, which limits their applicability and generalization capability in broader scenarios. To address this methodological rigidity, we propose a flexible framework for multi-modal feature fusion in biomolecular interaction prediction (FlexBIP). The core of FlexBIP lies in its modular architecture, whic
papers.summary: FlexBIP is a modular framework for predicting biomolecular interactions that decouples topological and molecular features, allowing flexible multi-modal feature fusion across diverse interaction types. This design enables the method to generalize across tasks and data modalities better than existing single-task, single-modality approaches.

papers.title: Comprehensive evaluation of AlphaFold/OpenFold prediction of experimentally unresolved proteins through novel metrics.
papers.abstract: Predicting accurate protein structures is essential for understanding molecular mechanisms, interpreting the impact of sequence variation, and supporting translational applications ranging from drug discovery to clinical genomics. Recent advances in deep-learning-based predictors such as AlphaFold2, OpenFold, and AlphaFold3 have transformed structural biology, enabling routine in silico modeling even for challenging or previously uncharacterized proteins. However, systematic benchmarking of these tools-especially for novel targets and single amino acid variants-remains limited. Conventional gl
papers.summary: This study systematically benchmarks AlphaFold2, OpenFold, and AlphaFold3 on experimentally unresolved proteins and single amino acid variants using novel evaluation metrics. It finds that while these deep-learning predictors perform well on many targets, accuracy varies for novel proteins and variant effects, highlighting limitations that conventional metrics miss. The work provides guidance for interpreting predicted structures in drug discovery and clinical genomics contexts.

papers.title: Ethical Considerations on Artificial Intelligence, Health and Health Care. All That Glisters Is Not Gold.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming global health care through innovations in deep learning, generative models and agentic AI systems. Traditional reductionist approaches to complex pathophysiological pathways fail to capture the true complexity of disease, motivating the adoption of network medicine (NM), which models biological systems as dynamic, interconnected networks. When combined with AI, NM enables integration of multiomic data and better characterizes disease mechanisms to guide precision therapies. Nevertheless, the rapid diffusion of AI in health care also raises profound
papers.summary: This paper discusses how artificial intelligence, combined with network medicine approaches, is transforming healthcare by integrating multiomic data to better model complex diseases and guide precision therapies. However, it emphasizes that the rapid adoption of AI in healthcare raises profound ethical concerns that must be carefully addressed. The authors caution that not all that appears promising in AI-driven healthcare is genuinely beneficial.

papers.title: Discovery of novel acridine based inhibitors of Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) via pharmacophore modeling and machine learning-driven virtual screening followed by molecular dynamic studies.
papers.abstract: Bruton's Tyrosine Kinase (BTK) has been recently recognized as an important drug design target for treating B-cell malignancies. Unfortunately, drug resistance is making the treatment of B-cell malignancies challenging. In this study, we employed a dual machine learning drug design approach that involves two parallel branches: the QSAR-GFA modeling (Branch 1) which engages the development of an interpretable structure activity relationships, and the KNIME® based machine learning modeling (Branch 2) which aimed at achieving high predictive accuracy. Subsequently, six machine learning modules, e
papers.summary: This study identifies novel acridine-based inhibitors of Bruton's Tyrosine Kinase (BTK), a key target in B-cell malignancies, using a dual machine learning approach combining QSAR modeling with KNIME-based predictive models. The workflow integrates pharmacophore modeling, machine learning-driven virtual screening, and molecular dynamics simulations to discover and validate candidate compounds. The findings offer new chemical scaffolds that could help overcome drug resistance in B-cell cancer treatments.

papers.title: Correction to: Structure-informed machine learning for drug discovery: a task-centric perspective.
papers.summary: This is a correction notice for a previously published review article titled 'Structure-informed machine learning for drug discovery: a task-centric perspective' in Briefings in Bioinformatics. It does not present new research findings, but rather corrects errors in the original publication. The correction likely addresses minor inaccuracies in the text, figures, or references.

papers.title: Decoding cancer with artificial intelligence: Transforming research, diagnosis, and therapy with future insights.
papers.abstract: Cancer remains one of the leading global health burdens, with increasing complexity in genomic, imaging, and clinical datasets presenting significant challenges for effective management. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful tool to address these challenges by enabling pattern recognition, knowledge integration, and data-driven decision-making. This review highlights recent advances in the application of AI across cancer research, diagnosis, and therapy. In research, AI accelerates drug discovery and repurposing, enhances genomic data interpretation, and facilitates biomarker
papers.summary: This review surveys recent advances in applying artificial intelligence across cancer research, diagnosis, and therapy, covering areas such as drug discovery and repurposing, genomic data interpretation, and biomarker identification. It argues that AI can help manage the growing complexity of genomic, imaging, and clinical datasets in oncology.

papers.title: A cross-species drug-discovery platform to accelerate the identification of lifespan-extending interventions.
papers.abstract: We develop an integrated, high-throughput platform to evaluate pharmacological lifespan-extending interventions across five model organisms spanning unicellular to mammalian biology including yeast, nematodes, fruit flies, killifish, and mice. By combining automated imaging, miniaturized assays, and deep-learning-based death detection, we evaluate over 400 compounds across thousands of conditions. In S. cerevisiae, a miniaturized PI/flow cytometry CLS assay enables scalable screening and identifies key assay confounders, while in C. elegans and D. melanogaster, compact imaging platforms couple
papers.summary: The authors built a cross-species drug-discovery platform that tests compounds for lifespan extension across yeast, nematodes, fruit flies, killifish, and mice, using automated imaging, miniaturized assays, and deep-learning-based death detection. Screening over 400 compounds across thousands of conditions, they identify candidate lifespan-extending interventions and highlight key assay confounders in yeast chronological lifespan assays.

papers.title: Predicting Single-Cell Perturbation Responses Across Biological Contexts With a Deep Generative Model Integrating Optimal Transport.
papers.abstract: Predicting how single cells respond to perturbations is a central problem in computational biology, with potential relevance to emerging artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC) research and drug-discovery efforts. However, substantial variation in perturbation responses across biological contexts and the limited generalizability of current models make prediction across cell types, patients, species, and other contexts particularly challenging. To address this challenge, we present single-cell perturbation inference via latent optimal transport (scPILOT), a query-conditioned framework for t
papers.summary: The authors present scPILOT, a deep generative model that integrates optimal transport to predict single-cell perturbation responses across diverse biological contexts such as cell types, patients, and species. By conditioning on query information, the framework aims to overcome the limited generalizability of existing models, supporting applications in virtual cell research and drug discovery.

papers.title: Molecular insights and ADMET profiling of iridoids as candidate leads for erectile dysfunction therapy.
papers.abstract: Erectile dysfunction (ED) significantly affects male psychosocial health and has an increasing incidence. Although phosphodiesterase 5 (PDEi-5) inhibitors are the first-line therapy, the occurrence of visual side effects resulting from cross-inhibition of the PDE-6 isoform limits their adoption. In this context, the plant Veronica anagallis-aquatica L. emerges as a promising source of bioactive therapeutic compounds. This work investigated the inhibitory potential and selectivity of eight iridoid glycosides from this species against PDE-5 and PDE-6. The results identified catalposide as the mo
papers.summary: This computational study screened eight iridoid glycosides from the plant Veronica anagallis-aquatica for their ability to inhibit PDE-5 (the target for erectile dysfunction treatment) while avoiding PDE-6 (whose inhibition causes visual side effects). Catalposide emerged as the most promising candidate, with molecular docking and ADMET profiling suggesting favorable selectivity and drug-like properties. The work proposes plant-derived iridoids as potential alternatives to current PDE-5 inhibitors like sildenafil.

papers.title: Bridging the AI Divide in Drug Discovery: Practical Lessons from Capacity Strengthening in Africa.
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become an integral part of drug discovery in high-income countries. However, these advances have yet to be broadly adopted by research ecosystems in many low- and middle-income countries in Africa, where understudied infectious diseases, compounded by a growing noncommunicable disease burden, cause millions of deaths each year. Given adequate support and appropriate models AI could play a transformative role in under-resourced biomedical research ecosystems in Africa, democratizing drug discovery research. There is an urgent need to invest in building the criti
papers.summary: This perspective article discusses the gap in AI adoption for drug discovery between high-income countries and African research ecosystems, where infectious and noncommunicable disease burdens remain high. It argues that with adequate support and context-appropriate models, AI could democratize drug discovery in under-resourced settings, and calls for investment in capacity strengthening.

papers.title: Accelerate Your Science: Direct-to-Biology Strategies in Medicinal Chemistry.
papers.abstract: Direct-to-biology (D2B) is a powerful strategy that accelerates early drug discovery. It enables compounds to be synthesized in miniaturized formats and evaluated directly as crude reaction mixtures. This bypasses the need for purification during the initial design-make-test cycle. Advances in robust synthetic methodologies, automation, reaction miniaturization, and biological screening have transformed D2B from a proof-of-concept approach into a versatile medicinal chemistry platform. This platform is applicable to fragment optimization, covalent ligands, macrocycles, proteolysis-targeting ch
papers.summary: This review describes direct-to-biology (D2B) strategies, where compounds are synthesized in miniaturized formats and screened directly as crude reaction mixtures, skipping purification in the early design-make-test cycle. Advances in synthesis, automation, miniaturization, and biological screening have turned D2B into a versatile platform applicable to fragment optimization, covalent ligands, macrocycles, and PROTACs. It highlights how this approach can substantially accelerate early drug discovery.

papers.title: Evaluating the outputs of ARAE-based molecular generative model for synthetic accessibility and BTK inhibition.
papers.abstract: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) methodologies in drug discovery represents a rapidly expanding area of interest, providing a valuable means for exploring uncharted chemical spaces to identify novel therapeutic candidates. In this proof-of-concept study, we evaluated hypothetical drug-like molecules generated by an adversarial regularized autoencoder (ARAE) architecture, which were not documented in existing chemical literature and databases, for their synthetic tractability and inhibitory effects on Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK). Utilizing a structure-based computational appro
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study evaluates drug-like molecules generated by an adversarial regularized autoencoder (ARAE) for their synthetic accessibility and ability to inhibit Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK). The authors use structure-based computational methods to assess whether AI-generated compounds are both synthesizable and biologically plausible, highlighting the practical challenges of applying generative models in drug discovery.

papers.title: Gaps in AI-Driven Pharmacokinetic Property Prediction for Early Drug Development: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Machine learning applications in preclinical drug development have been focused on automated covariate selection in pharmacometric modeling and high-throughput screening processes early in drug discovery. While inherent drug property prediction has made significant improvements in the past decade, fusing early target-based drug discovery methods to preclinical stage pharmacokinetic (PK) property predictions has been limited. This scoping review investigates the current state of PK property prediction of small molecules in drug discovery using machine learning methods and a combination of machi
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This scoping review surveys how machine learning is currently used to predict pharmacokinetic (PK) properties of small molecules in early drug development, finding that most work focuses on automated covariate selection and high-throughput screening rather than integrating target-based discovery with PK prediction. The authors highlight a significant gap: fusing early target-based methods with preclinical PK property prediction remains limited despite a decade of progress in drug property prediction.

papers.title: Three privileged scaffolds, one pipeline: chalcones, pyrazolines and pyrazoles in drug discovery and fluorescent sensing.
papers.abstract: Chalcones, pyrazolines, and pyrazoles constitute a uniquely powerful discovery pipeline in which each is a privileged scaffold with distinct applications, while also serving as the synthetic precursor to the next. Despite a theoretical chalcone library exceeding 680 000 unique structures accessible from commercial starting materials alone, fewer than 5140 examples have been reported in the literature-representing just 0.8% of this chemical space. Combining this precursor library with the downstream pyrazoline and pyrazole chemical spaces yields a combined landscape conservatively estimated to
papers.summary: This review highlights chalcones, pyrazolines, and pyrazoles as privileged scaffolds that form a sequential synthetic pipeline, where each serves as a precursor to the next. The authors note that despite a theoretical chalcone library exceeding 680,000 structures, only about 0.8% have been reported, indicating vast unexplored chemical space for drug discovery and fluorescent sensing applications.

papers.title: Evaluating the Incremental Value of Three-Dimensional Conformer Descriptors for Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Prediction Using the B3DB Benchmark Dataset.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Predicting blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability remains a major challenge in central nervous system (CNS) drug discovery. Three-dimensional (3D) conformer-derived molecular descriptors are often proposed as improvements over conventional two-dimensional (2D) topological representations; however, their incremental predictive value remains unclear. Methods: Here, we systematically evaluated six molecular feature sets comprising curated 2D Mordred descriptors, Morgan/ECFP4 fingerprints, 3D conformer-derived descriptors, and their combinations, using LightGBM regression on
papers.summary: This study systematically tested whether adding 3D conformer-derived molecular descriptors improves blood-brain barrier permeability prediction over conventional 2D descriptors and fingerprints. Using the B3DB benchmark and LightGBM regression across six feature sets, they assessed the incremental predictive value of 3D information. The findings clarify whether the added computational cost of 3D conformers is justified for CNS drug discovery.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in rheumatoid arthritis: current applications and future perspectives.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a highly prevalent systemic autoimmune disease characterized by a complex and partially understood pathogenesis. The substantial challenges in early identification and marked therapeutic heterogeneity pose a significant burden on affected patients. Despite notable advancements in diagnostic techniques and therapeutic interventions in recent years, optimal patient care remains hindered by several ongoing clinical challenges. To address these limitations, artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly integrated into the field of rheumatology. By leveraging its p
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence is being applied to rheumatoid arthritis, covering current uses and future directions. It highlights AI's potential to improve early diagnosis and address treatment heterogeneity in RA patients. The paper surveys the field and identifies ongoing clinical challenges that AI may help overcome.

papers.title: A comprehensive review of AI innovations for tackling antimicrobial resistance.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a major global public health concern, rendering available antimicrobials ineffective and leading to infections that are difficult to treat. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly applied across the AMR continuum, including resistance prediction, rapid diagnostics, new antimicrobial discovery, drug repurposing, antimicrobial surveillance, and clinical decision support. In this review, we aim to highlight recent developments in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to address antimicrobial resistance (AMR). In addition, we review computatio
papers.summary: This review surveys recent applications of artificial intelligence across the antimicrobial resistance landscape, covering resistance prediction, rapid diagnostics, discovery of new antimicrobials, drug repurposing, surveillance, and clinical decision support. It aims to consolidate how AI methods are being leveraged to combat the growing global challenge of drug-resistant infections.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-driven identification and mechanistic exploration of synergistic anti-aging compounds from Dengzhan Shengmai formulation.
papers.abstract: Aging is a complex biological process involving multiple dysregulated pathways, and synergistic compound combinations offer distinct therapeutic advantages through multi-target and multi-pathway interactions. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulations are inherently synergistic, yet systematically identifying their active anti-aging combinations remains a major challenge. Here, we developed DeepSMCA, a deep learning-based framework integrating molecular descriptors, ADMET parameters, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network embeddings learned via a variational graph auto-encoder (VGA
papers.summary: The authors developed DeepSMCA, a deep learning framework that combines molecular descriptors, ADMET properties, and protein-protein interaction network embeddings to identify synergistic anti-aging compound combinations from the traditional Chinese medicine formulation Dengzhan Shengmai. This approach offers a systematic way to mine multi-target synergistic effects from complex herbal formulations, moving beyond single-compound screening.

papers.title: In Silico Identification of Natural-Product Aromatase (CYP19A1) Inhibitors via Integrated Molecular Docking and QSAR Modelling.
papers.abstract: Aromatase (CYP19A1) is the rate-limiting enzyme in estrogen biosynthesis and the principal therapeutic target for estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer. Despite the clinical success of third-generation aromatase inhibitors (AIs) such as letrozole and anastrozole, acquired resistance and systemic adverse effects, including musculoskeletal pain, bone density loss, and cardiovascular complications, which necessitate the identification of novel scaffolds. This study employs an integrated computational pipeline combining ligand-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) mode
papers.summary: This study uses an integrated computational pipeline combining QSAR modeling and molecular docking to identify natural-product compounds that could inhibit aromatase (CYP19A1), a key enzyme in estrogen biosynthesis and a target for ER+ breast cancer therapy. The approach aims to find novel scaffolds that might overcome resistance and side effects associated with current aromatase inhibitors like letrozole and anastrozole.

papers.title: De Novo Molecular Design and Bioactivity Prediction of Novel Hexahydroquinolines as Plasmodium falciparum Calcium-Dependent Protein Kinase 4 (CDPK4) Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Plasmodium falciparum Calcium-Dependent Protein Kinase 4 (PfCDPK4) is a validated target for malaria transmission-blocking interventions, as its inhibition disrupts male gametocyte exflagellation. Hexahydroquinolines (HHQs) have emerged as promising gametocytocidal agents. This study aimed to design novel HHQs as potential PfCDPK4 inhibitors with good binding affinity, favourable pharmacokinetics, and structural stability. A library of 20,000 novel HHQ analogs was generated using genetic algorithm-driven de novo molecular design in AlvaBuilder and systematically filtered through a pipeline com
papers.summary: This study used genetic algorithm-driven de novo molecular design to generate 20,000 novel hexahydroquinoline analogs and screened them as potential inhibitors of Plasmodium falciparum CDPK4, a validated malaria transmission-blocking target. The compounds were filtered for binding affinity, pharmacokinetics, and structural stability, identifying promising candidates for further development. The work demonstrates a computational pipeline for designing gametocytocidal antimalarial agents.
